cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster, so it's made to be sung. A whole group speaks a blessing over one person facing a day of trouble, and they start with this: may the LORD answer you. It's like the group chat flooding you with prayer hands before your big day, except this group chat has a CHOIR.

cards.question: Next comes the name of the God of Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). What does the group hope that name will do for the person in trouble?

cards.text: Next they tell this person, "May He send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion." Help straight from God's own house, with no hold music and no 'please leave a message.'
Then they hope He'll remember every gift this person has given. This choir isn't skimming the file, friend: they're going through EVERY page.

cards.question: The group hopes the LORD will remember this person's gifts. True or false: they also hope He'll look favorably on this person's burnt offerings.

cards.text: Then a Selah lands right there in the song. After it, they tell this person they hope He'll give them the desires of their heart.

cards.question: The group hopes God will give this person the desires of their heart. What do they hope for this person's plans?
The group pictures the day this person wins. True or false: they hope they'll get to keep it quiet.

cards.text: They hope they'll get to shout for joy and raise a banner in the name of their God, like a whole stadium waving one giant flag. And they hope the LORD grants every request this person makes.

cards.question: Up to now, the psalm has been one 'may' after another. Then one voice says he knows it now: the LORD ___ His anointed.

cards.text: He's sure the LORD saves His anointed and answers him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand. Friend, MY right hand is half a mustache, and HIS right hand SAVES.
Then comes the big comparison: some trust in chariots, and others in horses. That's trusting horsepower, friend, and I have watched horsepower sit in rush hour traffic just like everybody else.

cards.question: The group praying in this psalm doesn't trust in chariots or horses: we trust in the ___ of the LORD our God.
The ones who trust in chariots and horses collapse and fall. True or false: the ones who trust in the name of the LORD fall right beside them.
The last line finally names the person this whole psalm has been praying for. Who is it?

cards.text: Then they turn to the LORD Himself and ask Him to answer them on the day they call. The song opened hoping the LORD would answer this one person, and it closes asking Him to answer all of them.
